rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): filter zero-event sessions from list endpoints
rawCommits.body:
The chats sidekick was rendering "New chat" rows that did nothing on
click. The recent commit 1aa47dd10 dropped the frontend filter that
hid summary-less rows on the assumption that the lazy-`+` refactor
guaranteed every row had at least one user message — but
`create_new_chat_session` runs *before* `persist_user_message` in
`apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/agents/chat/persist.rs`, so any
race or persist failure on the very first turn leaves an orphan
session with zero events. Plus there's pre-`lazy-+` legacy data in
storage from before the chat-input "+" became lazy. Both showed up
as `"New chat"` rows whose click navigated to `?session=<id>` and
rendered an empty transcript visually identical to the prior view.

Filter at the API: after collecting sessions in
`list_project_sessions` and `list_sessions`, fan out
`list_events?limit=1` per session via `futures::future::join_all`
and drop the rows whose probe returned an empty Vec. Probe errors
fail-open so a transient aura-storage hiccup never erases a real
chat. The helper is gated on a non-empty input so the typical
"empty list" case stays a no-op.

Tests cover the two endpoints (zero-event session filtered,
event-bearing session kept) and the fail-open path (probe 500s,
session preserved).

Front-end comments in `SessionsList.tsx` and `session-row-utils.ts`
are updated to point at the new server-side invariant — a
`NEW_CHAT_PLACEHOLDER` row now means "Haiku is mid-summary for a
real first turn", never "orphan empty session that does nothing on
click".

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: filter zero-event sessions from list endpoints

match across the placeholder-to-persisted swap. The prior turn's
assistant now keeps its key when a new user message is appended (no
forced unmount, no `useHighlightedHtml` / markdown / image
re-initialisation, no split-second gap until the new mount finishes
async work), while the existing end-of-turn stream-to-persisted
remount-free behaviour is preserved by the alias.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): heal null-org agents so first chat saves instead of 424'ing
rawCommits.body:
Legacy agents created before the UI started stamping `org_id` (and any
upstream record that drops the field) made `agent.org_id == None`. The
lazy auto-bind in `ensure_agent_home_project_and_binding` then returned
early at the org-guard, leaving the agent with no `project_agent` row,
which surfaced `chat_persist_unavailable` (424) on the user's first
chat turn with the message "target agent is not bound to any project
in storage [...] Call assign_agent_to_project before retrying."

Now the heal falls back to the caller's single org (via
`network.list_orgs`) when the agent itself has no `org_id`, and stamps
the binding row with the resolved id so downstream queries can scope
by org. Multi-org callers stay ambiguous on purpose -- silently picking
"first" risks binding a teammate's agent into the wrong org -- and
those still need `scripts/backfill_agent_orgs.ts` for repair.

Adds unit tests for the unambiguous-pick decision (single / multi /
zero org cases). Existing marker tests untouched.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): keep desktop chat input bar stable across session switches
rawCommits.body:
Clicking a different session in the agents-shell "Chats" sidekick used
to re-render the entire bottom chat input bar even though `streamKey`
(= `projectId:agentInstanceId`) is unchanged for same-agent navigation.
The bar is wrapped in `React.memo`, but several props it received were
referentially unstable: the panel-state reset effect handed it fresh
empty `attachments`/`selectedCommands` arrays, and `handleSend` /
`handleNewChat` / `handleCombinedStop` callbacks were re-created on
every render via deps that flipped per session.

This change holds those props stable per `streamKey`:

- Module-level `EMPTY_ATTACHMENTS` / `EMPTY_COMMANDS` reused on every
  reset, with early-return setter guards so the state writes are no-ops
  when already empty.
- `handleSend` reads `commands`, `selectedMode`, `pinnedSourceImage`,
  `isStreaming`, and `scrollToBottom` via refs; deps shrink to
  `[buildApiAttachments, streamKey]`.
- `handleNewChat` / `handleNewSession` read `markNextSendAsNewSession`
  and `historyKey` via refs.
- `maybeRenameFromFirstPrompt` reads its full context bag via a single
  ref so its identity is empty-deps stable; `wrappedSend` consequently
  becomes stable per `streamKey`.
- `handleCombinedStop` reads `loopOnlyBusy` via a ref.

A regression test in `ChatPanel.test.tsx` mounts the panel with one
`scrollResetKey`, records the input bar render count, then re-renders
with a different `scrollResetKey` (simulating a session click) and
asserts the count is unchanged - exercising the same shallow-prop
compare path that gates `React.memo` in production.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep desktop chat input bar stable across session switches

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): clear shared stream slot on cross-session click in agents shell
rawCommits.body:
Clicking a session row in the agents-app sidekick navigates to a new
?session= URL, which makes useAgentsShellTarget flip from `project` to
`placeholder` while the new session's events fetch. That swap unmounts
ProjectAgentChatPanel, then a fresh instance is mounted once the new
entry lands in chat-history-store. The panel's own `prevSessionIdRef`
cross-session cleanup can't see across the unmount/remount, so the
fresh mount re-initialises with the new sessionId and skips its
`resetEvents([])` early-return. Combined with `useChatHistorySync`'s
`streamCount >= historyMessages.length` hydrate guard, the new session
inherits the previous session's events from the shared
`${projectId}:${agentInstanceId}` stream slot — the "first click does
not load, second one does" report.

Move the cross-session reset up to the resolver, where the effect
survives the panel lifecycle and fires while the placeholder is up so
the next paint of the new project panel lands hot.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): inject agent personality into chat system prompt
rawCommits.body:
Both chat hot paths (`agent_route::send_agent_event_stream` and
`instance_route::send_event_stream`) used to forward only the agent's
`system_prompt` to the harness, silently dropping `name`, `role`,
`personality`, and `skills` on every interactive turn. The harness has
a parallel `build_agent_preamble` helper (used by the task-execution
path) but no equivalent runs for chat, so an agent edited via the UI's
PersonalityTab would never feel different in conversation.

Compose a small identity preamble in aura-os-server and prepend it to
the existing project-context block before handing the prompt to the
harness. No wire-protocol change; the harness still treats
`SessionConfig.system_prompt` as opaque.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): + new chat in agents shell no longer locks the lane on a blank placeholder
rawCommits.body:
Clicking the "+" button in the agents-app shell (`/agents/:agentId`)
strips `?session=` from the URL with the explicit intent of starting
a fresh chat. `useAgentsShellTarget` was mishandling that transition:
`urlTarget` could not resolve (no session in URL), `fallbackTarget`
still pointed at the just-abandoned `mostRecent` session, so the
resolver returned `kind: "placeholder"`. The default-session redirect
hook bailed out (`didDefaultRef` was already stamped from the prior
session render), so the URL never got a session re-added and the
chat lane stayed pinned to a blank `lanePlaceholder` div until the
user reloaded or clicked another session.

Teach the resolver to distinguish "cold load with no session"
(redirect imminent, keep placeholder) from "user just cleared the
session via +" (mount the standalone fresh-canvas panel) by latching
a `visitedSessionRef` whenever the URL has carried a `?session=` for
the current agent. After the next send, `handleSessionReady` writes
the new session id back into the URL and the resolver flips back to
`kind: "project"` so `ProjectAgentChatPanel` takes over.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): + new chat clears the lane and surfaces an optimistic "New chat" row in the sidekick
rawCommits.body:
Two follow-ups to the previous resolver fix so clicking "+" actually
delivers the ChatGPT-style fresh-canvas experience the user expects.

Chat lane: `ProjectAgentChatPanel.handleNewChat` only cleared its own
`session:p:i:s` key, but the URL flip means the next mount reads from
a different key. On the agents-shell route the resolver swaps to
`StandaloneAgentChatPanel`, which keys its history off
`agent:<orgAgentId>` and would otherwise refill via
`api.agents.listEvents` with the agent-wide event window — producing
"old messages on the fresh canvas". On the bare project route the
no-session `historyKey` flips to `project:p:i` and refetches via
`api.getEvents`. Now `handleNewChat` also clears both destination
keys and wipes the standalone stream slot (gated on `getIsStreaming`
so a live turn isn't clobbered) so the next mount lands hot on an
empty canvas. `useStandaloneAgentChat.handleNewChat` clears the
mirror project key for symmetry across the post-`SessionReady` URL
flip.

Sidekick: add an optimistic "New chat" placeholder row to
`useSessionsListStore` (`pendingNewChatBySurface` map +
`setPendingNewChat` / `clearPendingNewChat` actions, surfaced via
`useSessionsForSurface` and a new `usePendingNewChat` selector). The
chat-input "+" path now sets the placeholder; both `SessionReady`
handlers (`build-stream-handler.ts` for project chat,
`use-agent-chat-stream.ts` for standalone) clear it once the real
session id arrives. `ChatsTab` highlights the placeholder when the
URL has no `?session=`. `SessionsList` renders `_pending` rows with a
muted style, no context-menu delete, and `useSessionSummaries` skips
them so the synthetic id never 404s the summarize endpoint.

Tests: added 13 new tests across `AgentChatView`, `SessionsList`,
and `sessions-list-store` covering destination key clearing, stream
slot preservation mid-stream, placeholder rendering / selection /
deletion guards, and the per-surface lifecycle.

rawCommits.subject: Instrument silent attachment intake on desktop chat input.
rawCommits.body:
User reported that paste / drag-drop / + picker all silently fail to
render an attachment preview on /agents/<uuid>, in both Chat and Image
modes, with no console errors. Code-reading the desktop intake path
(handlePaste / handleDrop / fileInput onChange -> addFiles ->
processFile -> setAttachments -> AttachmentPreviews) didn't surface a
deterministic break, so this commit instruments every link with
[attach]-prefixed console logs so the next repro tells us exactly
which step drops the file.

Also hardens processImageFile / processTextFile with reader.onerror
handlers and try/catch around readAsDataURL / readAsText. Without
those, a FileReader failure (or a synthetic clipboard File the browser
can't fulfil) makes the inner Promise hang forever; Promise.all inside
addFiles then waits indefinitely and the entire intake silently
swallows. Each error path now resolves(null) and warns under [attach]
so we can spot it in the console.

Logs added:
- handlePaste / handleDrop entry + short-circuit reasons
- fileInput onChange entry
- addFiles entry, per-guard short-circuit reason, processed counts,
  onAttachmentsChange invocation, zero-valid warning
- processFile size-cap and unsupported-type rejections
- processImageFile / processTextFile FileReader errors and throws
- panel-level setAttachments (only when called via the
  onAttachmentsChange path, not internal resets)
- AttachmentPreviews render with current count

rawCommits.subject: Source agent bindings from server, not active-org sidebar
rawCommits.body:
The agents-app sidekick "Chats" tab and the standalone-agent default-
session redirect were deriving an agent's project_agent bindings by
walking `useProjectsListStore` — a snapshot scoped to the user's active
org. Older remote agents like Glenn / Machina that were auto-bound to
their per-org Home project (a project that may live outside the active
org's sidebar, and is created without Orbit fields) had a server-side
binding the client never enumerated, so the sidekick listed zero
bindings, the loader was gated by `!bindingsKey`, and the surface
rendered "No sessions yet" while real sessions sat in storage.

Fix: `loadAgentSessions` now fetches the authoritative binding list
from `GET /api/agents/:agent_id/projects` (the same source the chat
persistence pipeline uses on the server) into a new `bindingsByAgent`
map, and `useAgentBindingsKey` reads from there. Drops the
`!bindingsKey` short-circuit in `ChatsTab` and the standalone redirect
hook so the loader runs unconditionally on agent change. Adds
`useAgentBindingsLoadStatus` so `AgentChatView`'s shell-target picker
can render the `pending` lane while the binding fetch is in flight,
instead of flashing the fresh-canvas standalone view for agents that
actually have prior chats.

rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): patch optimistic row in setSessionSummary instead of bumping version
rawCommits.body:
The previous fallback (bump `version` when no row matched the incoming
session id) raced SSE `SessionReady`'s `replaceSessionId` swap. When
the on-send title generator finished before the harness emitted
`SessionReady` (Haiku ~800 ms vs harness boot ~1.5 s), `bumpVersion`
triggered `loadAgentSessions` which returned the new row with its real
id and freshly-persisted title. `preserveOptimisticRows` then carried
the still-optimistic placeholder forward, leaving two rows visible:
the real one with "What Is A Cat" and the optimistic one still
showing "New chat".

Patch any pending optimistic placeholder rows in the same surfaces
instead. `replaceSessionId` rewrites only `session_id` and preserves
every other field, so the title survives the swap and `SessionReady`'s
own `bumpVersion`-driven load reconciles cleanly without a second
refetch racing the swap.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): keep prior assistant bubble aliased when send appends a new user message
rawCommits.body:
`applyTailIdAliases` walks `prev` and `curr` tail-aligned to alias the
prior assistant's `stream-...` placeholder to its persisted event id
across the end-of-turn swap. When the user pressed Send in the same
render that swap landed, `curr` grew by one (the freshly appended
`temp-` user bubble), the tail walk compared `prev`'s assistant
against `curr`'s new user prompt, mismatched on role, and broke
before the alias could be recorded. The assistant's React key flipped
from `stream-...` to its persisted id, React remounted the bubble,
and the user saw the previous assistant get overwritten for a frame
before reappearing once the next turn finished.

Skip trailing `curr` entries whose id is neither present in `prev`
nor already aliased before starting the tail-aligned walk so the
placeholder->persisted alias survives across an append.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep prior assistant bubble aliased when send appends a new user message

rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): stop title events from stamping unrelated optimistic rows
rawCommits.body:
`setSessionSummary` matched any optimistic row in the surface, not
just the placeholder for the session whose title arrived. When the
user clicked "+" and sent a second chat before Title-1 finished
generating, the late-arriving Title-1 event would patch the still-
in-flight `opt-2` placeholder alongside `real-1`. After
`replaceSessionId` swapped `opt-2 -> real-2` the row carried the
wrong title and rendered as a duplicate of `real-1` until refresh
re-fetched server-persisted summaries.

Drop the optimistic-row arm and stash the summary in a new
`pendingSummariesById` map keyed on the real session id.
`replaceSessionId` reads (and clears) the entry when swapping, so a
title that lands before SessionReady still attaches to the right row
the moment we know the optimistic placeholder maps to it - no cross-
contamination across concurrent new-chat creates.

Also drop any pending entry on `removeSession` so deleted sessions
don't leak summaries forever.

rawCommits.subject: fix(release): flip cargo default to stable-channel so the updater can't silently ship dead
rawCommits.body:
The two-job release pipeline introduced in 718a47c6b silently shipped
dev-channel binaries to users between May 5 and May 6. Dev-channel
disables the in-app updater (`Channel::current().updater_enabled() ==
false` for Dev), so every entry point in `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/updater/`
early-returns and the binary never checks for updates. The follow-up fix
in 6122ad6ef added `--no-default-features --features stable-channel` to
the release workflows, but already-installed broken builds cannot recover
themselves — `updater_supported()` is gated by a `cfg!`-baked channel
constant — so users on nightly.472 or earlier need a manual reinstall.

Make the failure mode fail *closed* by flipping the cargo default from
`dev-channel` to `stable-channel` on `aura-os-desktop` and
`aura-os-server`. After this change, plain `cargo build -p aura-os-desktop`
produces a stable binary; if a workflow regression ever drops the
explicit `--features stable-channel` flag again, the result is still
stable rather than a silently-broken dev binary that ships to users.

Dev runners (`scripts/dev/run-desktop-dev.sh`, `run-desktop-dev.ps1`,
`run-mobile-dev.sh`) now pass `--no-default-features --features
dev-channel` to cargo so they keep producing dev builds with parallel-
but-distinct identifiers (data dir name, ports, single-instance mutex,
window title, skills tree) that can run alongside an installed stable
AURA. Release workflows keep their explicit
`--no-default-features --features stable-channel` flags as
belt-and-suspenders to encode intent and survive future default flips.

`crates/aura-os-core/Cargo.toml` already defaults to `stable-channel`,
so no change there. Update the README channel-selection paragraph and
the "Run desktop app (live dev)" section to match the new behavior.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): reinstate prior assistant when send-frame merge drops it
rawCommits.body:
The first attempt at this regression (91c47d4e1) only fixed the React
key-stability path: it kept `applyTailIdAliases` from remounting the
prior assistant bubble when its placeholder->persisted id swap landed
in the same render that appended a new optimistic user prompt. That
addresses one specific race but the user still observes "sending a new
message removes the last message for a split second then it pops back."

Static analysis of every merge input (`useStreamEvents`, message-store
thread, history-store events, `combineStoredAndStreamMessages`,
`applyTailIdAliases`) couldn't pin the symptom to a single race. There
are at least three independent ways the prior assistant can briefly
vanish during a send: a WS-driven force refetch returning a mid-persist
snapshot before the new turn's MessageEnd, an LRU eviction of the
shared per-(project, instance) stream entry, and an in-flight
`invalidateHistory` clearing the message-store thread between the
optimistic stream append and the next render.

Rather than chase each race independently, enforce the end-state
invariant in `useConversationSnapshot`: when the merged result ends
with an optimistic local user prompt — the canonical "user just hit
Send" frame — and the previous-frame cache for the same transcriptKey
carries persisted entries that are now missing from the merge, splice
them back in chronological order before the trailing optimistic prompt.

The reinstate path is gated on the trailing optimistic-user invariant,
so idle (between-turn) refreshes — including legitimate server-side
deletions that drop a prior assistant from history — pass through the
no-op branch and trust the merge result. Cached optimistic ids are
never reinstated; we only restore persisted ids whose disappearance
mid-send is structurally suspicious.

Two tests cover the fix:
1. The reinstate path: simulate a force-refetch race that drops the
   prior assistant from both stored and history while a follow-up
   `temp-2` lands in the stream. Without the splice the merged tail
   is `[user-1, temp-2]`; the fix restores `[user-1, asst-1, temp-2]`.
2. The non-trigger guard: an idle refresh that drops the prior
   assistant (no optimistic user prompt at the tail) must NOT
   resurrect the assistant — proving the splice respects legitimate
   server-side state changes.

rawCommits.subject: fix(updater): preflight macOS read-only / translocated bundles + offer one-click recovery
rawCommits.body:
cargo_packager_updater::Update::install on macOS fails with
`Read-only file system (os error 30)` (EROFS) whenever the running
Aura.app sits on a read-only mount -- the most common cause being
Gatekeeper Path Randomization ("App Translocation"), which serves
the bundle from a randomised firmlink under
/private/var/folders/.../AppTranslocation/. The upstream crate only
falls back to `osascript ... with administrator privileges` for
ErrorKind::PermissionDenied, and EROFS is a different ErrorKind, so
the user sees an opaque "Stopped at: Install Inner Started" mid-
install with no actionable guidance.

This was always going to fail (it has been latent since the
auto-install commit on Mar 30) but only became visible after the
diagnostics overhaul on May 4 surfaced step labels prominently.

Detect the condition up front and surface a real recovery flow:

- New `updater::bundle_path` module classifies the running bundle
  (translocated / read_only / on_dmg) using path inspection plus
  libc::statfs(2) MNT_RDONLY on macOS.
- New UpdateStep variants (BundlePathResolved, PreflightFailed,
  RelocateRequested/Spawned/Failed) leave a complete forensic trail
  of every install attempt's resolved bundle path + filesystem
  flags in updater.log, so any future read-only failure mode that
  is *not* App Translocation (mounted DMG, MDM-managed
  /Applications, ...) is also identifiable from the on-disk record.
- perform_update_install + start_install run the preflight before
  building the updater so a read-only-mount install fails fast
  with an actionable message instead of consuming bandwidth only
  to fail at Update::install.
- New macOS-only relocate_and_relaunch_macos runs an authenticated
  `osascript ... with administrator privileges` ditto + xattr -dr
  com.apple.quarantine + atomic mv into /Applications, then
  `open -n` and exits. Quarantine is cleared on the destination so
  the relocated bundle is *not* re-translocated on the next launch.
- New endpoints GET /api/update-bundle-info and
  POST /api/update-relocate-and-relaunch expose the inspection +
  recovery to the renderer; both refuse on non-macOS or for
  bundles that are already in a writable location.
- UpdateControl renders a macOS-specific recovery card (in both the
  inline and panel layouts) when bundleInfo indicates the read-only
  condition: plain-language explanation of App Translocation, the
  resolved bundle path, "Move to /Applications and relaunch"
  primary action, "Reveal in Finder" secondary action, and the
  existing "Show updater logs" affordance.

Tests: bundle_path classification (translocation, /Volumes,
/Applications, ~/Applications, blocks_in_place_update predicate)
and a new UpdateControl Vitest suite covering the recovery card
rendering, button wiring, pending state, and panel layout.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): prefetch destination history on hover to stop chat-lane flicker
rawCommits.body:
Switching agents in either the agents shell or the projects shell briefly
revealed `ChatPanel`'s cold-load reveal cycle: the input bar stayed put
while the message area went `visibility: hidden` and a fading overlay
flashed before the new transcript appeared. The cause was that the
chat-history-store entry for the destination key (`session:p:i:s` or
`project:p:i`) was `idle` at click time, so `historyResolved` flipped
false on the first render and re-armed the gate.

Warm the destination chat-history-store entries proactively:
- `AgentList` hover and the desktop sidebar-mount worker now chain
  `loadAgentSessions` + `fetchHistory(sessionHistoryKey(...))` so the
  most-recent project session for each visible agent lands as `"ready"`
  before the click. (`prefetchHistory` only warmed React Query, not the
  store the panel actually reads.)
- `SessionsList` exposes a new `onSessionHover` hook, wired by both the
  agents `ChatsTab` and the projects `SessionList` to `fetchHistory` the
  per-session events on row pointer-enter.
- `ProjectList` (zui Explorer) delegates `onMouseOver` from the wrapping
  div to look up the hovered agent row and warm both the no-session
  `projectChatHistoryKey` and the most-recent session entry.

Also gate `useChatHistorySync`'s `invalidateBeforeFetch` path on the
entry's freshness — without this, `invalidateHistory` would clobber
`fetchedAt=0` immediately after the prefetch and re-trigger the flicker.
The follow-up `fetchHistory` still runs, so cross-tab freshness is
preserved.

Promotes `sessionHistoryKey` from `AgentChatView` to `chat-history-store`
so prefetchers and the panel agree on the cache key shape.

hook returning a discriminated-union `ConversationTarget`, plus a
sibling `usePreviousReadyTarget` that holds the prior panel across

stable `markNextSendAsNewSession` via `useCallback`, eliminating two

rawCommits.subject: refactor(chat): stable clientId keys + pure conversation projector
rawCommits.body:
Replaces the brittle "merge three transcript stores" pipeline with a
single source of truth for React reconciliation: every DisplaySessionEvent
carries a stable `clientId` from the moment it is created.

Changes:

- Add `clientId?: string` to DisplaySessionEvent. ChatMessageList now keys
  on `clientId ?? id`, so the bubble does NOT unmount/remount when the
  temp- placeholder id is swapped for a persisted event_id at end of turn.
  This removes the entire `applyTailIdAliases` walk that previously
  compensated for the same race after the fact.

- Assign `clientId` at every creation site:
  * buildUserChatMessage (optimistic user)
  * lifecycle.handleAssistantTurnBoundary (stream placeholder)
  * lifecycle.finalizeStream / handleStreamError (terminal frames)
  * lifecycle.handleEventSaved (default = event_id)
  * mergeSavedAssistantMessage preserves the original placeholder's
    clientId across the temp- -> event_id swap
  * buildDisplayEvents (hydrated history rows)

- Introduce `shared/lib/conversation-projector.ts` as the single pure
  function that merges history + stream into the displayed transcript.
  Single-pass strategy:
    1. Take history wholesale.
    2. Drop stream rows whose id is already in history.
    3. Drop an optimistic temp- user only when it exactly matches the
       *immediately trailing* unanswered user in history (so a content-
       equal new prompt after an assistant reply is preserved).
  Includes focused unit tests in conversation-projector.test.ts.

- Collapse `useConversationSnapshot` from ~525 lines of anchor rules,
  `reinstateMissingPersistedOnSend` backstop, and `lastNonEmptyRef`
  flicker guards down to a thin wrapper that calls projectConversation.
  Old snapshot test file removed; coverage moves to the projector tests
  and the existing ChatMessageList tests (now updated to the clientId
  contract).

Net: -1134 lines, no new render-time hacks, identical visible behavior
with stable React identity end-to-end.

of the same transcript, and the second copy needed an entire

when the post-stream forced refetch raced with server persistence.

Changes:

- AgentChatPanel: pass `hydrateToStream: false` (matching the path
  StandaloneAgentChatPanel already used). Both consumers now render
  straight from the chat-history-store snapshot via
  useConversationSnapshot's pure projector.

- useChatHistorySync: remove the `hydrateToStream` option entirely
  and delete the ~80-line "Sync fetched history into the stream store
  for rendering" effect. The remaining clear-on-catch-up effect is
  refocused as a memory-pressure release (the projector handles
  visual deduplication; this just frees the stream store entry).

- helpers.ts: delete STREAM_FINISH_GRACE_MS — the race it guarded
  against is now structurally impossible because we no longer overwrite
  stream events with history snapshots.

- useConversationSnapshot: drop the unused `liveAssistantHasContent`
  selector that was carried for forward-compat with a deferred store
  rewrite. Projector signature trimmed to `(history, stream)`.

- use-standalone-agent-chat: drop the now-redundant
  `hydrateToStream: false` flag (it was the only behavior).

- Tests: convert the legacy "hydrates by default" expectation into a
  documentation comment + a positive "never hydrates ready history
  into the stream store" assertion. Strip remaining `hydrateToStream`

race surfaces, single source of truth for transcript rendering.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): close optimistic-row title clobber + leaked-row revisit races
rawCommits.body:
Two regressions surfaced after the agent-chat refactor:

1. New session stays "New chat" — Haiku title never sticks. The
   bumpVersion() that fires on SessionReady kicks off a fresh
   loadProjectSessions / loadAgentSessions; if the session_summary_updated
   WS event lands first, setSessionSummary patches the row AND stashes
   the title in pendingSummariesById, but the load then writes the
   server's empty-summary row over it — pendingSummariesById was only
   ever consulted by replaceSessionId, so the cached title was orphaned.
   Fix: applyPendingSummariesToList in both loaders so cached titles
   re-attach to the materialized row, and dropAppliedEntries trims the
   cache once each entry has been planted.

2. "Bad Request" when revisiting a session created during this chat. If
   the panel tore down before SessionReady (navigated away mid-stream,
   stream aborted, etc.), the optimistic placeholder leaked into
   sessionsBySurface. preserveOptimisticRows kept it across loads, and
   useMostRecentSession / useDefaultProjectSessionRedirect picked it as
   the redirect target — priming ?session=optimistic:... and 400ing the
   next history fetch.
   Fixes:
   - useMostRecentSession + mostRecentForInstance now skip rows whose
     id starts with OPTIMISTIC_SESSION_ID_PREFIX.
   - useOptimisticSessionRow now sweeps any non-swapped pending row
     from both surfaces on unmount, eliminating the leak at the source.

Tests: load-after-WS keeps the title, server-non-empty wins over a stale
cache entry, useMostRecentSession skips optimistic rows, the project
default-redirect picks the next non-optimistic candidate, and the
optimistic-row hook cleans up on unmount before swap.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): single-writer session URL + controlled sessions list
rawCommits.body:
Three user-visible bugs all fed off the same root: multiple writers
racing for the agent chat surface's `?session=` and a remount of the
ZUI Explorer on every selection change. This consolidates the writers
to a single resolver-owned redirect, makes the Explorer's selection
controllable, and adds defense-in-depth against an `optimistic:` id
ever leaking into a history fetch.

- vendor/zui Explorer: expose a controlled `selectedIds` prop
  (the underlying `ExplorerProvider` already supported it). Lets
  callers drive selection from external state without keying the
  Explorer to remount its DnD context on every click.
- SessionsList: drop the `${bucket}:${sessionId}` Explorer key hack
  and pass a memoized `selectedIds={[selectedSessionId]}` instead.
  Session rows are now referentially stable across selection changes,
  removing the flicker that swallowed the second click in the agents
  and projects sidekicks.
- useConversationTarget: become the single writer of `?session=` for
  the project route. The duplicate `useDefaultProjectSessionRedirect`
  call inside `AgentChatPanel` is removed and the hook itself
  deleted; the resolver short-circuits when `?session=` is already
  pinned (was previously clobbering explicit older-session clicks
  with "most recent for instance"). Defense-in-depth: an
  `optimistic:` value in the URL is treated as missing so the
  redirect can replace it before `api.listSessionEvents` would 400
  on the synthetic id.
- sessions-list-store: generalize `preserveOptimisticRows` to
  `preservePendingRows`. After `replaceSessionId` swaps an
  optimistic placeholder for a real id, a stale `list_sessions`
  response can arrive without the new id (server filters
  zero-event sessions and persistence may still be in flight).
  The store now carries forward any local row newer than the
  newest server-known row, bounded by a TTL so authoritative
  server deletes still win out.
- Tests: Explorer controlled-selection coverage (no remount on
  selection change), SessionsList no-remount regression,
  conversation-target explicit-click guard + optimistic-URL
  defensive coverage, and sessions-list-store real-id preservation
  + stale-row drop tests.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): highlight optimistic New chat + drop stale placeholders

Two related polish fixes layered on top of the controlled-selection
SessionsList refactor.

- SessionsList now falls back to the optimistic `optimistic:<uuid>`
  row when no `?session=` is pinned. After the user clicks `+` the
  URL holds no real session id until SessionReady streams back, so
  without this fallback the just-inserted placeholder visibly sits
  at the top of the list with nothing reading as selected — the
  user has no visual confirmation that their first send will land
  in this new chat. Reuses `isOptimisticSessionId` from the store
  so the placeholder convention stays in one place.
- `preservePendingRows` now drops an optimistic placeholder whose
  `started_at` is older than the newest server-known row for the
  same `(projectId, agentInstanceId)` binding. Without this, a
  leaked placeholder (panel torn down before SessionReady or
  cleanup ran) could survive indefinitely as a sibling to a newer
  real session. Bounding by binding (rather than across the whole
  list) avoids accidentally pruning a placeholder for a different
  agent that legitimately predates the server's newest row.
- Added regression tests for both behaviors.

rawCommits.subject: fix(installer): use MUI_CUSTOMFUNCTION_GUIINIT instead of bare .onGUIInit
rawCommits.body:
MUI2 auto-generates its own `.onGUIInit` from MUI_PAGE_* macro expansion,
so the AURA-added `Function .onGUIInit ... FunctionEnd` collided with it
and makensis aborted on `Function named ".onGUIInit" already exists`.

Switch to the documented MUI2 hook: register a custom function name via
`MUI_CUSTOMFUNCTION_GUIINIT` and rename our function to `AuraOnGUIInit`
so MUI's generated `.onGUIInit` calls us from there. Update the file's
re-sync notes so future upstream merges don't regress this.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(installer): use real MUI2 hook for welcome/finish show callback
rawCommits.body:
`MUI_WELCOMEFINISHPAGE_CUSTOMFUNCTION_SHOW` is not a real MUI2 define; both
Welcome.nsh and Finish.nsh call `MUI_PAGE_FUNCTION_CUSTOM SHOW`, which only
reads `MUI_PAGE_CUSTOMFUNCTION_${TYPE}`. The previous wiring meant
`AuraThemedWelcomeShow` was never invoked, so the runtime LoadImageW swap
that compensates for MUI's per-page GUIInit re-extracting the dark sidebar
bitmap never ran (and the dark-mode title bar fix on the inner dialog was
also dead).

Switch to `MUI_PAGE_CUSTOMFUNCTION_SHOW` and re-define it before BOTH
MUI_PAGE_WELCOME and MUI_PAGE_FINISH, since `MUI_PAGE_FUNCTION_CUSTOM`
`!undef`s the symbol after each consumption. Update the AURA-modifications
header to reflect the corrected hook.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rendered.title: New chat flow rebuilt and the macOS updater learns to recover itself
rendered.intro: A heavy day on the chat surface: the "+" new-chat experience was rebuilt end to end, session sidekick rows are now optimistic and live-titled, and a long-standing chat-bubble flicker on send was finally root-caused with a stable clientId rewrite. On the platform side, the macOS updater can now detect read-only / translocated bundles and offer one-click recovery, the Windows installer follows system light/dark mode, and a quietly-broken release default that had been shipping dev binaries to users was closed off.

entries.title: New-chat lane rebuilt: optimistic sidekick rows, live titles, and stable session switching
entries.summary: A long evening of work on the agents shell turned the "+" button into a real ChatGPT-style fresh-canvas flow, with optimistic placeholders, live-streamed session titles, and a host of session-switching races finally closed.

items.text: Clicking "+" now reliably clears the chat lane and surfaces an optimistic "New chat" row in the sidekick that swaps to the real session id (and live-streamed title) the moment SessionReady arrives — fixing the "first click does nothing, second one works" behavior and the blank-placeholder lock-up.

Session summaries are now generated as short, human-readable 2–5 word titles the moment the first prompt is persisted, pushed live to the sidekick over the event bus so rows flip from "New chat" to e.g. "Cyberpunk Character Design" before the assistant finishes streaming. The Haiku summarizer prompt was also made content-agnostic so trivial chats no longer get titled with refusal prose.

Chat bubble flicker on send is fixed: the prior assistant message stays mounted across the placeholder→persisted swap via an id-alias map, and a snapshot reinstate path keeps it from disappearing for a frame when send-time merges drop it. The desktop chat input bar also no longer re-renders on session switches thanks to stable, ref-backed callbacks.

Backend session list endpoints now filter zero-event sessions so orphan "New chat" rows from failed first turns disappear, and chat now actually injects the agent's name, role, personality and skills into the system prompt so PersonalityTab edits are felt in conversation. Legacy null-org agents also self-heal on first chat instead of returning 424.

entries.title: Release channel default flipped to stable so the updater can't silently ship dead
entries.summary: A latent regression had been shipping dev-channel binaries — which disable the in-app updater — to real users. Cargo defaults now fail closed.

items.text: Flipped the cargo default on aura-os-desktop and aura-os-server from dev-channel to stable-channel so a plain `cargo build` produces a stable, updater-enabled binary; release workflows keep their explicit `--features stable-channel` flags as belt-and-suspenders. Dev runner scripts now opt into dev-channel explicitly so local development still gets a parallel, isolated build.

entries.title: macOS updater recovery, themed Windows installer, and a from-scratch chat projector
entries.summary: The morning-into-evening session paired big platform fixes (translocation-aware updater, light/dark NSIS installer) with a structural rewrite of how chat transcripts are reconciled, eliminating an entire class of flicker bugs.

items.text: macOS updater now preflights the running bundle and detects App Translocation / read-only mounts before install, surfacing a recovery card in Org Settings with a one-click "Move to /Applications and relaunch" flow (authenticated ditto + quarantine clear + atomic move) instead of the opaque mid-install EROFS failure users were seeing.

The Windows NSIS installer now reads AppsUseLightTheme and swaps to light header/sidebar bitmaps when the system is in light mode, and enables DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE for a dark title bar in dark mode (Win10 1809+). Bitmap assets are vendored alongside a generation script.

Replaced the brittle three-store transcript merge with a stable `clientId` on every DisplaySessionEvent and a single pure `conversation-projector` — net −1134 lines, no more `applyTailIdAliases` walks, no more STREAM_FINISH_GRACE_MS race guard, and identical visible behavior with stable React identity end-to-end. The 1157-line AgentChatView was also split into focused components (AgentChatRoute, AgentChatPanel, StandaloneAgentChatPanel, ProjectAgentSwitcher) and hooks.

Agent and session switching is now flicker-free: hovering an agent or session row prefetches destination history into the chat-history-store, the previous panel stays mounted while the resolver is pending, and the sessions sidekick uses the ZUI Explorer's new controlled-selection mode so rows no longer remount on every click.

Chat image attachments are more forgiving: per-file 5 MB and total 10 MB caps that silently rejected uploads are gone, the server now persists `source_url` alongside base64 so images survive history reload, thumbnails no longer disappear after upload, and S3 + IAM bootstrap scripts ship for the production assets bucket.

Optimistic placeholder rows no longer leak into routing or get clobbered by stale loads: cached titles re-attach to materialized rows, optimistic ids are kept out of `?session=` and history fetches, and the sessions list visually distinguishes selected from hovered so the per-day Explorer no longer looks like it's multi-selecting across date buckets.

Plain `cargo run -p aura-os-desktop` is once again a Dev build (separate window title, data dir, ports, single-instance mutex) so developers can run debug alongside an installed stable AURA — released installers remain safe because every release path passes `--features stable-channel` explicitly. A read of partitioned harness memories also lands so MemoryTab returns the right data.

entries.title: S3 deploy scripts hardened for missing creds and Windows shells
entries.summary: The new S3 setup tooling now fails loudly on misconfiguration and works correctly under Git Bash on Windows.

items.text: S3 setup and IAM-user scripts verify AWS credentials up front, parse `create-access-key` output with sed (dropping the python3 dependency that broke under Git Bash on Windows), and only swallow the benign "bucket already owned" error so real misconfiguration surfaces instead of silently continuing.

entries.title: Sidekick highlights the new chat row the instant "+" is pressed
entries.summary: A small but meaningful follow-up so users get immediate visual confirmation when starting a new chat.

items.text: Inserted the optimistic session placeholder when "+" is pressed (rather than at first send) so SessionsList's optimistic-fallback branch can immediately highlight the new-chat row; arm() is idempotent so double-clicking "+" doesn't stack rows.

entries.title: Windows installer template fixes so the themed NSIS wizard actually builds and runs its hooks
entries.summary: Three follow-up fixes to the new themed NSIS template — required for the installer to compile under cargo-packager's Handlebars renderer and for the dark-mode hooks to actually fire.

items.text: Escaped literal `{{...}}` examples in NSI comments so cargo-packager's Handlebars renderer no longer chokes on Tera-style pipe syntax, and surrounding doc references to `{{header_image}}` / `{{sidebar_image}}` no longer get silently substituted with bitmap paths.

Replaced the bare `.onGUIInit` function with `MUI_CUSTOMFUNCTION_GUIINIT` registering `AuraOnGUIInit`, so it no longer collides with MUI2's auto-generated `.onGUIInit` and aborts makensis with "Function already exists".

Switched the welcome/finish page show callback to the real `MUI_PAGE_CUSTOMFUNCTION_SHOW` hook (re-defined before each page since MUI `!undef`s it after consumption), so the runtime sidebar bitmap swap and dark-mode title-bar attribute on the inner dialog actually run.

highlights: Rebuilt new-chat lane with optimistic sidekick rows and ChatGPT-style auto-titles
macOS updater preflights translocated bundles and offers one-click relocate
Stable clientId projector kills the assistant-bubble flicker on send
Windows NSIS installer now matches system light/dark theme
Release channel default flipped so dev builds can't silently ship to users
